newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - RUGBY UNION - Blues edgy ahead of Brumbies clash.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - RUGBY UNION - Blues edgy ahead of Brumbies clash.

text.p: AUCKLAND, April 11 - The Auckland Blues are training with an edge, the fear of losing motivating players as they look to Saturday's Super 12 rugby clash against the ACT Brumbies, NZPA reports.
For the first time this season Auckland put themselves through an All Blacks-style uncompromising run at Pukekohe Stadium last night, venue for tomorrow's top-of-the-table clash.

"We've probably been a bit complacent so far, but now is the time for us to lift our game. We've been a bit bitchy at training and that's because we're nervous," halfback Ofisa Tonu'u told NZPA after a tense two-hour workout yesterday.
"We might be a little under strength, but that is no excuse because we've got quality players who can come in and do the job just as well."

Auckland will be without tighthead prop Olo Brown and both first choice locks Robin Brooke and Richard Fromont. But their rearranged pack with Jim Coe and Leo Lafaiali'i at lock trained with vigour as they ran their moves decisively.
"We've worked on a lot of things such as the things we need to do on and off the ball and what they are likely to do," Tonu'u said.
"We have to cut down all their moves, especially their magic man Mr Knox (first five-eighth David Knox) and their halfback George Gregan.
"It is a combination of the pair that works for them, they go well with each other but if we cut one down then the other may not operate."
It is inevitable that having played All Blacks No 1 Justin Marshall (Canterbury) last week that Tonu'u would be compared to Australian test half Gregan ahead of tomorrow's game.
"From what I've seen George Gregan is playing really well, he is a world class player so you do expect that. I do have a lot of respect for him," Tonu'u said.
"It doesn't bother me that I played Justin Marshall last week and play George Gregan tomorrow. We have our own set standards as players.

"It is important that you look at their (ACT) key individuals, but if you focus too much on one person ... and I think a lot of people made a match-up last week (against Marshall), then you're taking your mind off the game plan.

"Last week I was trying to play to the team plan. I have to say that I don't think the team as a whole was up there in terms of mental preparation, but we came away with a win (29-28) and we're happy with that."
Tonu'u said he was happy with the way he played against Marshall last weekend at the same venue, but the more important aspect was that he kept his mind on the team plan.
"If I'd gone out there and let my mind detract from doing a job for the team then we could have lost that game," he said.
"I think we all know how badly we played last week, but we got out of jail and we hopefully won't let that happen from now on.
"If we play like that against sides like ACT and Transvaal we'll get a hiding."
Teams -

Auckland Blues: Adrian Cashmore, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Ofisa Tonu'u, Zinzan Brooke (captain), Mark Carter, Jim Coe, Leo Lafaiali'i, Michael Jones, Craig Dowd, Sean Fitzpatrick, Paul Thomson. Reserves: Michael Scott, Jeremy Stanley, Andrew Blowers, Dylan Mika,
Orcades Crawford, Richard Kirk.

ACT Brumbies: Stephen Larkham, Mitch Hardy, James Holbeck, Joe Roff, Pat Howard, David Knox, George Gregan, Troy Coker, Brett Robinson (captain), David Giffin, John Langford, Owen Finnegan, Ewen McKenzie, Marco Caputo, Patricio Noriega. Reserves: Rod Kafer, Geoff Logan, Ipolito Fenukitau, Justin Harrison, Timote Tavalea.
